provenance.cleanupNotes: Raw generated alpha threshold64 yields exactly eight distinct body components in two rows; raw has a warm glow (mostly alpha<64) and pose3 overlaps the nominal adjacent column by47px. Cleanup preserves source pose pixels, assigns generated fringes to nearest component, crops complete figures, uniformly fits each to264x360, and centers in row-major 384x512 cells. Raw glow and source margins were rejected; no redraw, duplication, or mirroring.

review.sourceNotes: Accepted cleaned sheet: eight ordered distinct complete Piper poses, right-facing consistent identity and anatomy, blank russet-red/cream kit, no ball, clean alpha with no glow on light/dark proofs, and >=60px fully transparent margin on all cell edges. Tick5 contact reach has open spread fingers clear of head/ponytail; frame8 settled stance distinct from initial ready pose.

provenance.ballBehavior: No ball is painted into the athlete sheet. Piper-specific contact path is height [1.05,1.0,.75,1.5,1.3,1.1,1.0,.95], forward [4,7,10,12.5,10,8,6,5]. Direct steals release into loose-ball physics at tick5; pass interception can carry from the tick5 hand contact.

nativeReview.notes: With the fixed native renderer setting both `anim` and `animation`, frame3 contact passes: the separate ball edge meets the open reaching fingertips in both facings and zooms without obscuring the hand. After a successful direct steal, gameplay releases ownership and uses loose-ball physics; a pass interception can carry the ball from the same hand position. Earlier fallback and candidate tracks are preserved as calibration previews but are not accepted.

review.notes: All eight production frames select at both zooms and facings. Independent native review confirms Piper-specific separate-ball contact at frame3/tick5, with loose-ball transition after direct steal.
